# Volume 3 — Chapter XIII The Way of Transgressors

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Robin and Lucy had gotten prepared to attend Sunday School. They were making the trip by themselves, a circumstance that occurred infrequently, because Mrs. Sowerby invariably went to Sunday School. However, Mrs. Sowerby had injured her ankle by twisting it and could not walk easily, which meant she was remaining at home on this particular morning. The twins were additionally expected to serve as the family's representatives at church, since Nell had departed the previous evening to pass Sunday alongside friends residing in Delford, while Thirza was suffering from a headache.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0000 }

Robin descended the stairs with slow steps. Lucy, whom Mrs. Sowerby had gotten prepared, was in the hall waiting for him. Robin had taken care of his own preparations. A cent was in his pocket for the collection at Sunday School, along with a five-cent piece for the church collection; one of his hands held his Bible while the other held his Sunday School quarterly; his lesson, his Golden Text, and his catechism question were known by him perfectly. Had he not been forced to study them in the kitchen of Mrs. Sowerby, during the entirety of the previous Sunday afternoon? Robin ought to have possessed a placid state of mind, consequently. In reality, text and catechism notwithstanding, his inner self resembled a ravening wolf.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0001 }

As he went to Lucy, Mrs. Sowerby came limping out from her kitchen.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0002 }

“Are you clean?” she asked with severity.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0003 }

“Yes—every part of me that is visible,” answered Robin, scowling in defiance.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0004 }

A sigh escaped Mrs. Agatha. Regarding the neck and ears of Robin, she harbored her doubts. She was aware, however, that Robin would probably run off if she tried to inspect him herself, and giving chase was beyond her today.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0005 }

“Well, make certain you conduct yourselves properly,” she cautioned them. “Avoid walking through dust. Avoid halting on the porch to converse with additional children. Avoid squirming or wriggling in your seats. Avoid forgetting the Golden Text. Avoid losing your collection money or failing to deposit it. Avoid whispering while prayers are said, and avoid failing to focus on the sermon.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0006 }

Robin did not condescend to answer. With the submissive Lucy trailing behind, he stepped off down the path. Yet his inner spirit raged. Robin had endured, or believed he had endured, numerous grievances from the actions and words of Mrs. Agatha Sowerby ever since her arrival at Grey Shutters, because Mrs. Sowerby was incapable of sharing a home with anyone, regardless of whether they were nine or ninety, without attempting to train them correctly. Furthermore, it was merely the prior afternoon when she had stepped in to persuade Thirza not to permit Robin to go angling alongside the Timothy Cottons. Robin remained furious about this.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0007 }

The moment he cleared the lane, Robin halted and contorted his face into an expression so unearthly and terrifying that Lucy, despite being familiar with his talents for doing so, felt genuine panic that he might remain stuck like that forever.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0008 }

“Darn her,” Robin exploded.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0009 }

“Oh, Robin, don’t swear,” Lucy gasped in dismay.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0010 }

“‘Darn’ is not a swear word—at least not a genuine one. Even if it were, it wouldn't matter to me,” Robin shot back impetuously.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0011 }

“Well, if you have to utter terrible words, please refrain from doing so on Sunday,” begged Lucy.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0012 }

Although Robin remained quite distant from feeling remorse, within his hidden heart he sensed that his actions might have slightly exceeded the proper limits.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0013 }

“I will create a curse word for myself,” he stated.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0014 }

“God will penalize you should you perform that,” Lucy stated in a serious manner.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0015 }

“In that case, I believe God is a cruel old rascal,” Robin shot back. “Is He unaware that a guy needs a method for ’spressing his emotions?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0016 }

“Robin!!!” exclaimed Lucy, anticipating that he would be instantly struck down dead where he stood; however, no such thing occurred.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0017 }

“At any rate, I am not going to endure another bit of Mrs. Sowerby’s bossing,” sputtered Robin. “Nell and Thirza might possess the right to order me around, but she lacks it. I intend to perform every last thing that she instructed me not to do. Just watch me.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0018 }

In severe, quiet intentness, as Lucy observed him with horrified enchantment, Robin walked off the green roadside turf, sinking to his ankles in the powdery dust that a month without rain had created on the highway, and proceeded forward through it, stamping his feet fiercely until a murky fog shrouded him.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0019 }

“That is the start,” he declared with victory. “And I intend to delay in the entryway and chat for as long as there is anyone present to converse with. I plan to twist and fidget and murmur, and I intend to state that I am ignorant of the Golden Text. And I am about to discard each of my collections at this very moment.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0020 }

And with intense pleasure, Robin flung the cent and nickel across the fence belonging to Mr. Pembroke.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0021 }

“It was Satan who drove you to do that,” Lucy said in a reproachful tone.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0022 }

“He didn’t,” Robin exclaimed with indignation. “I merely figured it out on my own. Furthermore, I’ve come up with another idea. I will not be attending Sunday School or church whatsoever. Instead, I’m heading up to play with the Cottons. Yesterday, they mentioned to me that they wouldn't be going to Sunday School today, since their mother was out of town and no one was forcing them to go. Come on, Lucy, we’re going to have a wonderful time.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0023 }

“I do not wish to go,” Lucy objected.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0024 }

“You must,” Robin said. “I will inform Thirza that you were kissed by Frank Bell at school this past Monday if you fail to come.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0025 }

“I was unable to prevent it. His actions were unknown to me in advance,” exclaimed Lucy, turning bright red.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0026 }

“Well, you failed to slap him or appear even slightly annoyed,” Robin snapped back. “If you refuse to come, I will report that to her as well. We will use the short cut across this field.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0027 }

“I am terrified of those cows,” poor Lucy objected, perceiving a chance to get away.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0028 }

“To think that you would be afraid of those cows,” Robin mocked. “After all, you are older than either of them.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0029 }

“They are larger,” Lucy remarked.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0030 }

“They will not harm you. Come on, right now. It is fantastic. I am not going to take the trouble to attend church whatsoever when I am older. I reckon that I am able to reach heaven on my own.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0031 }

“Violating the Sabbath day will send you to the other place,” remarked miserable Lucy, who trailed behind him extremely reluctantly.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0032 }

However, Robin felt no fear—so far. The torments of hell remained exceedingly distant, whereas the pleasures of going fishing alongside the Cottons were extremely close at hand. He desired that Lucy possessed greater courage. She continuously glanced behind her as though she might burst into tears at any second, which ruined a boy's enjoyment. Girls were a nuisance, regardless. On this occasion, Robin refrained from thinking "darn", even mentally. He felt no regret—so far—for having uttered the word a single time, though he reasoned it was wise not to push the Unknown Powers excessively in a single day.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0033 }

The young Cottons, who were outdoors in their rear yard, greeted the arrival of Robin with joyful shouts. Pete, Tommy, Adolphus, and Mirabel Cotton had no company, since their mother and elder sisters had left. Lucy felt grateful that Mirabel, at minimum, was present, having worried about being the sole girl among numerous boys. Mirabel acted nearly like a boy—being remarkably loud, tanned, and daring; nevertheless, she did wear dresses.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0034 }

“Going fishing is why we’re here,” declared Robin.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0035 }

“Whoop,” shouted the Cottons. Mirabel heading the front with a tin container, they hurried off immediately to unearth worms. Lucy was on the verge of sitting down to weep. Oh, if that detestable Frank Bell had simply not kissed her! Robin could have been defied by her then, and she could have attended her cherished Sunday School.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0036 }

Naturally, they did not dare to fish upon the pond, since folks traveling to church would spot them there. Instead, they were forced to use the stream located in the forest behind the Cotton home. It swarmed with trout, however, and they enjoyed a wonderful morning—or at least the Cottons definitely did, and Robin appeared to as well. Retaining a small measure of caution, he had removed his stockings and boots to put on a pair of Tommy Cotton’s overalls. Clad in this manner, he feared neither marsh, bog, nor brushwood. Lucy was openly and obviously wretched. As she trailed behind the rest of the group from one pool to another, she held her Bible and quarterly close to her chest, bitterly pondering her cherished class where she ought to be seated at that exact minute, in front of a beloved teacher. Instead of that, she found herself wandering through the forest alongside those semi-savage Cottons, attempting to shield her pretty white frock from tears and smudges while keeping her boots spotless. Mirabel had proposed lending her an apron, but Lucy had rejected the offer with disdain.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0037 }

The trout took the bait just like they always do on Sundays. Within an hour, all the fish they desired had been caught by the transgressors, who then went back to the house, which was a great relief to Lucy. As the rest engaged in a noisy game of tag, she sat in a proper manner on a hencoop in the yard; and after that, every one of them went up to the roof of the pig-house and carved their initials into the saddleboard. Robin received yet another idea from the henhouse with its flat roof and a heap of straw under it. They had a marvelous thirty minutes going up onto the roof and leaping down into the straw while uttering whoops and yells.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0038 }

Yet even illicit enjoyments cannot last forever. Robin realized they had to leave once the sound of wheels rolling across the pond bridge indicated that the congregation was returning from church. Ditching Tommy's overalls and putting his own proper clothes back on, he turned from his line of trout and sighed. Taking them back to the house was out of the question.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0039 }

“Well, didn’t we have a wonderful time?” he asked in a challenging way, while they walked down the field on the hill.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0040 }

“I had not,” Lucy stated in a flat tone. “And I do not believe you had—truly—either,” she inserted, experiencing a sudden burst of intuition that was uncharacteristic of her.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0041 }

“I did so,” Robin exclaimed, though sounding like someone who protests excessively. “It is no surprise you didn’t—simply perched there such as a—such as a mule.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0042 }

“I have no intention of associating with the Cottons,” Lucy declared in a superior manner.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0043 }

“The Cottons are fine,” Robin replied. “Moreover, their lives are much more enjoyable than ours. They act precisely as they wish and speak their minds openly in front of anyone. From now on, I intend to do the same.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0044 }

“You wouldn’t have the courage to mention many of those matters in front of the whole group,” Lucy declared.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0045 }

“No, there is not.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0046 }

“There is, as well. Would you,” Lucy inquired with seriousness, “would you utter ‘tomcat’ in front of the minister?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0047 }

This came as a complete shock. Robin had not anticipated a demonstration of free speech that was quite so tangible. However, consistency was unnecessary when dealing with Lucy.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0048 }

“Naturally I did not,” he conceded with a sullen air.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0049 }

“The term ‘Tomcat’ carries no sacred meaning. I would refrain from bringing up a creature like that in front of a minister altogether.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0050 }

“However, if it were necessary for you to?” Lucy pressed on.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0051 }

“I’d label it a Thomas pussy,” Robin remarked.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0052 }

“It would be more courteous to say ‘gentleman cat,’ I believe,” Lucy pondered.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0053 }

“You thinking!” Robin fired back, her voice dripping with biting contempt.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0054 }

Robin felt far from at ease, even if he would rather lose his life than confess as much to Lucy. His conscience was starting to grant him beneficial pricks of guilt, now that the excitement of his forbidden pleasures had faded. It might have been preferable to attend Sunday School and church, when all was said and done. Mrs. Sowerby could be domineering; nevertheless, a container of biscuits remained in her kitchen pantry and she lacked any meanness. Robin recalled at this awkward juncture that Mrs. Sowerby had expertly repaired his new school trousers when he ripped them the previous week, and she had refrained from uttering a single word regarding the matter to Thirza.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0055 }

However, the limit of Robin’s wrongdoing had still not been reached. He would soon learn that concealing a single misdeed requires committing a second one. That afternoon, they dined alongside Mrs. Sowerby, who began by inquiring of Robin,
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0056 }

“Was everyone from your Sunday School class present today?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0057 }

“Yes’m,” Robin uttered, swallowing hard. “Every single one was present—save for one.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0058 }

“Have you recited your catechism and Golden Text?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0059 }

“Yes’m.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0060 }

“Was your collection included by you?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0061 }

“Yes’m.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0062 }

“Did Mrs. Malcolm MacKinnon attend the service?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0063 }

“I don’t know.” The miserable Robin reflected that this, at minimum, was true.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0064 }

“Did they announce the Ladies’ Aid for the coming week?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0065 }

“Yes’m”—fearfully.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0066 }

“Was prayer-meeting?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0067 }

“I—I’m not sure.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0068 }

“It ought to be known to you. More careful attention should be paid by you to the announcements. What did Mr. Harvey’s text say?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0069 }

Robin hurriedly gulped down some water, gulping away his final pangs of guilt alongside it. An old Golden Text he had memorized a few weeks prior was glibly repeated by him. Mrs. Sowerby luckily ceased her interrogation of him at that point; nevertheless, the meal held no pleasure for Robin.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0070 }

A single portion of pudding was all he was capable of eating.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0071 }

“What is wrong with you?” asked the rightly amazed Mrs. Sowerby. “Are you ill?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0072 }

“No,” whispered Robin.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0073 }

“You seem pale, so you ought to stay in the shade later today,” Mrs. Sowerby advised.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0074 }

“Do you realize the number of untruths you uttered to Mrs. Sowerby?” Lucy inquired with a tone of reproach, the moment they found themselves by themselves following dinner.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0075 }

Driven to desperation, Robin spun around with ferocity.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0076 }

“I do not know and I do not care,” he stated. “Just keep quiet, Lucy Farrow.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0077 }

Afterward, the unfortunate Robin retreated to a hidden spot situated past the stack of wood so he could reflect on the path of sinners.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0078 }

Darkness and silence enveloped Grey Shutters at the time Nell arrived home. Because she was extremely weary and drowsy, she went to bed immediately. Late hours had been required by various Brierley celebrations during the previous week. Scarcely had Nell placed her head on her pillow when she was half asleep; however, at that exact moment, her door opened gently and a entreating voice said, “Nell.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0079 }

Sleepily, Nell sat upright.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0080 }

“Robin, can that be you? What has happened?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0081 }

An individual dressed in white threw themselves across the floor and onto the bed.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0082 }

“I am extremely happy that you have returned, Nell,” Robin wept as he wrapped his arms around her neck. “I was unable to fall asleep before sharing this with a person.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0083 }

“What did you tell somebody?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0084 }

“How wretched I feel.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0085 }

“What is making you unhappy, my love?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0086 }

“Since I acted so terribly today, Nell. Oh, I behaved dreadfully—worse than I ever have before.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0087 }

“What did you do?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0088 }

“Oh, telling you frightens me. My dear Nell, you will cease to like me forever. Tonight, my prayers remained unsaid. What I had done could not be spoken to God. The thought of Him knowing filled me with shame.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0089 }

“Yet Robin, He was aware regardless.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0090 }

“Lucy said that. However, I believed he might not have seen it right then, perhaps. Regardless, my preference was to inform you first.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0091 }

“What was your action?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0092 }

Everything spilled forth all at once.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0093 }

“I fled from Sunday School—and I went angling alongside the Cottons—and I uttered ever so many falsehoods to Mrs. Sowerby—oh! nearly six—and—and—I—I uttered a profanity, Nell—or something almost like a profanity, at least—and I hurled insults at God.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0094 }

Quietness descended. Robin was uncertain how to interpret this. Could Nell be in such state of shock that she would refrain from talking to him ever again?
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0095 }

“Nell, what will you do with me?” he murmured.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0096 }

“It is nothing, my dear. My belief is that your punishment has already occurred.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0097 }

“I haven’t, no. They haven’t done anything to me.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0098 }

“Ever since you committed that wrong, you have been extremely unhappy, haven’t you?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0099 }

“You bet!” Robin said with emphasis.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0100 }

“It was your conscience that was penalizing you, Robin.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0101 }

“I want to understand what my conscience is.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0102 }

“There is a quality inside you, Robin, which invariably informs you whenever you act improperly and causes you to feel miserable if you continue doing so. Have you not observed that?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0103 }

“Indeed, though I was unaware of its nature. I would rather be without it. My enjoyment would be much greater. In what place is my conscience, Nell? My desire is to find out. Does it reside within my stomach?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0104 }

“No, your soul holds it,” Nell replied, grateful that the gloom concealed her face, because solemn occasions required one to keep a straight countenance.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0105 }

“I reckon I can’t escape it, in that case,” Robin uttered with a sigh. “Will you inform Thirza and Mrs. Sowerby about my actions, Nell?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0106 }

“No, my love, I will not inform a soul. You feel regret for your misbehavior, do you not?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0107 }

“You bet!”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0108 }

“And you will not act badly like that ever again.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0109 }

“No, but—” Robin inserted guardedly, “I could be bad in a different manner.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0110 }

“You will not utter bad language, or escape on Sundays, or speak lies to conceal your wrongdoings?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0111 }

“No. There is no money in it,” Robin said.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0112 }

“Well, Robin, simply inform God of your regret and request His forgiveness.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0113 }

“Are you no longer angry with me, Nell?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0114 }

“Certainly, my love.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0115 }

“In that case,” Robin stated with delight, “it matters little to me if God feels inclined to or not.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0116 }

“Robin!”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0117 }

“Oh—I will pray to Him—I will pray to Him,” Robin uttered rapidly, hurrying down from the mattress, persuaded by the sound of Nell’s voice that his words had been terrible. “It does not bother me to pray to Him, Nell.—I beg You, God, I am terribly remorseful that I conducted myself poorly today and I will endeavor to act properly on Sundays forever and I beg You to pardon me.—See that, Nell.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0118 }

“Well, now, go along to bed like a good boy.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0119 }

“Very well. Listen, I no longer feel mis’rubul. I feel great. Good night.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0120 }

“Good night.”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0121 }

Nell slid lower against her pillows, exhaling a sigh that brought relief. Oh—she was—so weary! Within a moment—
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0122 }

“Nell!” Robin had returned to the side of her bed. Nell forced her eyes to open.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0123 }

“What is it now, dear?” she inquired, attempting to prevent a tone of impatience from slipping into her voice.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0124 }

“Nell, has it ever caught your attention the way Mr. Pettifer spits? If I work at it with all my might, do you s’pose I can manage to spit in that exact same way?”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0125 }

Nell sat up.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0126 }

“Robin Farrow,” she declared, “head directly to your bed and ensure I do not see you out of it for the rest of the night! Move, right now!”
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0127 }

Robin departed, making no delay in the manner of his leaving.
{: #nw-v03-c13-p0128 }
